subtopics.title: Comparative Performance Evaluation
subtopics.summary: Ranking models against each other to determine which is better, without measuring absolute quality or whether a model is good enough for a specific use case.

subtopics.title: Absolute Performance Evaluation
subtopics.summary: Evaluating a model against fixed criteria or thresholds to determine its actual quality and whether it meets the requirements for a given application.

subtopics.title: Limitations of Comparative Evaluation
subtopics.summary: Comparative rankings do not reveal absolute performance; a model can win against another while both are bad, both good, or one good and one bad, making it unclear if a swap is worthwhile.

subtopics.title: Scalability Bottlenecks in Comparative Evaluation
subtopics.summary: Comparative evaluation is data-intensive because the number of model pairs grows quadratically with the number of models, requiring large numbers of comparisons for reliable rankings.

subtopics.title: Lack of Standardization and Quality Control
subtopics.summary: Challenges in ensuring consistent and reliable evaluation signals when using human or AI judges, including variability in voter quality and the need for evaluation guidelines and rubrics.
